subject: Renewal: reserved capacity increase to 32 GPUs — pricing & SLA proposal

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal: reserved capacity increase to 32 GPUs — pricing & SLA proposal

Hi Julia,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, Ataplan's current Dedicated pool (16 GPUs) is up for renewal on 2027-01-15. Given the Q1 product ramp you described, attached is a straightforward renewal + expansion proposal to move to a 32-GPU reserved pool with a production throughput guarantee.

Two paths on the table (attached workbook for blended math):

1) Immediate 32-GPU reserved commitment (12 months) — simplest operationally.
   - Per-GPU reserved rate (hourly): $1.35/hr
   - Throughput guarantee: sustained pool throughput of 300k tokens/sec (aggregate) with a 99th percentile tail latency target we can iterate on with your SREs.
   - Implementation notes: dedicated pool migration scheduled during off-peak window; prefix caching preserved.

2) Stepped commitment (preferred if finance needs ramp): 16 -> 24 (month 1) -> 32 (month 3) with blended pricing and a 3-month credit during step-up.

Next steps I recommend:
- If path (1) works, please confirm by 2026-12-12 to lock the quoted per-hour rate and Q1 onboarding credits.
- If procurement needs a PO template or SOC2, I can loop Marissa and SE to expedite.

Attachments: Redwood_AR_16to32_pricing_workbook.xlsx (workbook), SOW_32GPU_draft.docx (SOW draft).

If you want a short call this week to walk the workbook I can take 20 minutes — otherwise happy to get a PO and we’ll circulate the DocuSign.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 14:20:45 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: reserved capacity increase to 32 GPUs — pricing & SLA proposal

Ben / Karthik —

Looping in to coordinate commercial approvals and technical SLAs. Summary of what Julia asked for: lower per-hour target (~$1.20/hr) and a clearly scoped throughput SLA. Procurement also asked for SOC2 and PO template (they attached one).

My suggested counter:
- Commit to $1.30/hr per GPU for a 12-month reserved commitment if Ataplan signs by 2026-12-12. This leaves room to add a one‑time onboarding credit equal to 1 week of reserved hours (applied on first invoice) in lieu of deeper immediate discount.
- For the SLA: propose we put the following in the SOW (draft attached):
   * Sustained aggregate throughput: 320k tokens/sec across the reserved pool (measured at the edge/prefix cache aggregation point).
   * Availability/latency commitment: 99.9% availability for the reserved pool; p99 tail latency target for 4k context under synthetic benchmark < 180ms.
   * Remedies: service credits up to one month of reserved fees for repeated SLA misses (3+ incidents in a rolling 90-day period).

If Karthik confirms feasibility of the latency/throughput targets on our current stack (quantization + batching profiles), I think moving to $1.30 with the onboarding credit is an acceptable commercial outcome and keeps us protected on margin.

Attachments: SOW_32GPU_draft.docx (SOW redline).

Marissa Cole
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Julia Park <julia@ataplan.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 10:37:13 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal: reserved capacity increase to 32 GPUs — pricing & SLA proposal

Hi all —

Technical confirmation from SE side: the proposed throughput SLA is achievable with the following guardrails and operational commitments from both sides:

- Workload profile: benchmarks performed at 4k context, mixed prompt/streaming generation, median token production rates similar to what Julia shared. If the mix shifts heavily to long-context retrieval + generation we need to rebaseline.
- Runtime profile and optimizations: enable continuous batching + prefix KV caching. We recommend the 4-bit quantized variant for memory headroom on the 32-GPU pool (we can ship a compatibility matrix).
- Monitoring & alerting: Redwood will provide per-route token throughput dashboards and 1-minute aggregation. We will also add a runbook to the SOW for incident triage and an on-call escalation path.

Commercially, given the operational runway and the onboarding credit Marissa proposed, I support $1.30/hr for a 12-month commitment if signed by 2026-12-12.

Redwood proposed pricing math for clarity (monthly):
- 32 GPUs * 24 hrs/day * 30 days = 23,040 GPU-hrs/month
- At $1.30/hr => $29,952/month reserved fee (billed monthly)

I've attached a redline to the SOW that explicitly calls out measurement points for throughput and the incident thresholds for SLA credits.

Karthik Iyer
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Attachment: SOW_32GPU_draft-redline.docx
